bull.b: The return to positive earnings after losses in 2022–2024 indicates a meaningful improvement in operating execution and earnings power. A positive EBIT margin gives SelectQuote greater capacity to fund operations, invest in productivity, and withstand moderate pressure on revenue or commissions.

Positive operating and free cash flow provide tangible support for the turnaround, while the $60M fiscal 2027 target establishes a durable internal funding objective. Stronger cash generation could help reduce high-cost debt, support preferred dividends, and improve capital allocation flexibility.

Permanent cost reductions and increasingly embedded AI workflows can improve unit economics beyond a single reporting period. Better call routing, coaching, and agent productivity should support scalable customer acquisition and help protect margins as SelectQuote pursues growth.

bear.b: A material revenue decline weakens operating leverage and makes the profitability recovery more dependent on cost control. Persistent top-line pressure can limit reinvestment, reduce commission opportunities, and make it harder for improved margins to translate into sustained earnings growth.

The Inflation Reduction Act creates a multi-year headwind for Healthcare Services revenue, limiting the usefulness of simple year-over-year comparisons and extending uncertainty around growth. Even with manufacturer reimbursements offsetting EBITDA impact, lower reported revenue can constrain scale.

A deliberately smaller agent base reduces near-term selling capacity and limits the number of policies SelectQuote can place, even if productivity per tenured agent improves. Lower volume can constrain commission revenue and make growth recovery more dependent on market conditions and hiring.
